extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of travel/natural-history prose; travelers and informed Victorian-era general readers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit standards for composing first‑hand travel and natural‑history accounts: emphasise accuracy, vivid concrete description, verifiable evidence, and balanced judgement when assessing people, institutions, and antiquities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not describe what you have not yourself seen
rubrics_metrics.description: It is altogether contrary to the plan of this book to describe what I have not myself seen; but, having been led to mention them, I felt bound to do something to call attention to these marvellous works of art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit detailed descriptive claims to things personally observed; if referring to second‑hand accounts, signal that status and keep descriptions brief. Avoid inventing or elaborating on hearsay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use verifiable details when making critiques or accusations
rubrics_metrics.description: Every statement of this kind is thickly interspersed with italics and capital letters; but as the names are all fictitious, and neither dates, figures, nor details are ever given, it is impossible to verify or answer them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When exposing abuses or making strong claims, provide names, dates, figures, and specific details so readers can verify or evaluate the charge; absence of such particulars weakens credibility (anti‑pattern: rhetorical emphasis without facts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Test prosperity and governance by population increase
rubrics_metrics.description: There is, however, one grand test of the prosperity, and even of the happiness, of a community, which we can apply here--the rate of increase of the population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use census and demographic data (with dates) as a key empirical measure when judging the effects of governance or policy; give comparative figures and compute rates to make the point concrete (example: census numbers and percent increases provided for Java).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize abuses as exceptions and consider historical causes
rubrics_metrics.description: The oppressive and servile relations between chiefs and people, which have continued for perhaps a thousand years, cannot be at once abolished; and some evil must result from those relations, until the spread of education and the gradual infusion of European blood causes it naturally and insensibly to disappear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing systemic problems, acknowledge long historical causes and distinguish ordinary operation of a system from abuses due to individual misconduct or transition effects; avoid attributing every ill to the system alone without nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance praise and criticism; avoid one-sidedness
rubrics_metrics.description: With our usual one-sidedness in all relating to the Dutch Colonial System, this work has been excessively praised... Greatly to my surprise, I found it a very tedious and long-winded story...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present balanced judgement: recognise both merits and faults of people, institutions, or works; wary of popular or fashionable verdicts that may be one‑sided (anti‑pattern: uncritical praise or unverified denunciation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer first-hand, sensory, and measurable description
rubrics_metrics.description: The bricks are exceedingly fine and hard, with sharp angles and true surfaces... The central dome is fifty feet in diameter; around it is a triple circle of seventy-two towers...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete sensory detail and measurable dimensions (sizes, counts, distances) to convey scale and material reality. Specific numbers and tactile/visual descriptors make scenes more convincing and vivid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comparisons to familiar references to convey scale and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of human labour and skill expended on the Great Pyramid of Egypt sinks into insignificance when compared with that required to complete this sculptured hill-temple...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare unfamiliar subjects to well‑known landmarks, places, or cultural references to help readers grasp magnitude or significance; comparisons can be historical, geographic, or cultural.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve and record antiquities: governments should act
rubrics_metrics.description: It is much to be regretted that the Dutch Government does not take vigorous steps for the preservation of these ruins from the destroying agency of tropical vegetation; and for the collection of the fine sculptures which are everywhere scattered over the land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for active preservation and systematic collection/recording (photography, excavation, cataloguing) of antiquities before they are lost; use the writer's platform to call for institutional action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt collecting methods to local seasonal and environmental conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The weather was exceedingly hot and dry, no rain having fallen for several months, and there was, in consequence, a great scarcity of insects, and especially of beetles. I therefore devoted myself chiefly to obtaining a good set of the birds...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When engaged in fieldwork, be flexible: change focus and methods according to local conditions (e.g., shift from insects to birds when insects are scarce). Report such methodological choices transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include human anecdotes and local customs to illustrate character
rubrics_metrics.description: They were conducted by two priests to a bench... the ceremony of circumcision was then performed... A boy had been killed and eaten by a tiger... The Waidono had got together about seven hundred men, and were in chase of the animal...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use well‑chosen anecdotes, rituals, trials, and local incidents to bring communities and character to life; such stories serve both illustration and ethnographic interest (but remain sensitive and factual).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report practical travel information and costs for the reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Travelling in Java is very luxurious but very expensive... the only way being to hire or borrow a carriage, and then pay half a crown a mile for post-horses... the lowest charge is five guilders (8s. 4d.) for half a day...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include useful logistical details (modes of transport, costs, changing stations, accommodation arrangements) to help readers plan travel and to ground narratives in practical reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not over-generalize from anecdote; prefer aggregated evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: It is said that the Residents, desirous of showing a large increase in the products of their districts, have sometimes pressed the people to such continued labour... If this has happened, it is certainly not a common thing, and is to be set down to the abuse of the system...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting alleged abuses or trends, indicate whether claims are isolated or widespread; distinguish anecdotal reports from systematic patterns, and attribute uncertainty where verification is lacking.
